scope: Original environment proposals for the 25 priority fidelity identities; not generated images or canonical scene certification.

saturnin_duck.location: Miniature village washhouse beside a narrow duck-sized stream
saturnin_duck.foreground: Wet pebble bank, a fallen willow leaf and a shallow wooden washing tub scaled to a real duckling.
saturnin_duck.midground: A small plaster washhouse with timber posts, cloth on a low line and a footbridge across the stream.
saturnin_duck.background: Hand-built village cottages and soft real foliage, with practical miniature-set depth rather than a drawn fantasy town.
saturnin_duck.lighting: Gentle overcast daylight with soft natural reflections in the water.
saturnin_duck.sourceContext: Les Aventures de Saturnin, ORTF 1965-1970: real yellow duckling photographed in a miniature animal village. This washhouse arrangement is an original scene compatible with the production method, not a certified episode set. No clothing or human anatomy added; episode props still require photographic comparison.

lilo_pelekai.location: Open-sided Hawaiian hula practice pavilion overlooking a garden on Kauai
lilo_pelekai.foreground: Bare wooden floorboards, a woven mat and Lilo’s small camera beside Scrump; plenty of clear space around her sandals.
lilo_pelekai.midground: Low railing, broad open doorway, stacked dance mats and a single potted tropical plant.
lilo_pelekai.background: Dense hibiscus garden, low palms and a distant green ridge, rendered in the 2002 animated film’s painted environment language.
lilo_pelekai.lighting: Warm morning sun filtered through roof beams, with cool garden shadows.
lilo_pelekai.sourceContext: Lilo & Stitch, animated film 2002: child Lilo in her red white-leaf dress. Original quiet hula-related scene on Kauai; pavilion geometry is invented, not presented as a reconstructed film shot. Preserve her film design and ordinary personal props.

stitch_626.location: Red-earth garden path under the exterior deck of the Pelekai hillside home
stitch_626.foreground: Large fern leaves, red soil and a small chewed wooden offcut emphasize Stitch’s short size.
stitch_626.midground: Raised house supports, weathered exterior steps and a coiled garden hose beneath the deck.
stitch_626.background: A sloping tropical garden opens toward pale ocean and the low roofline of the house.
stitch_626.lighting: Late-afternoon gold through leaves, with a cool shaded space below the deck.
stitch_626.sourceContext: Lilo & Stitch, animated film 2002: Experiment 626 in the two-visible-arm Earth dog disguise. Original domestic garden composition inspired by the film setting; no claim of a matching frame. Do not add the separate four-arm alien presentation or a humanoid costume.

mj_performer.location: Original copper-and-indigo rehearsal ballroom with a sprung dance floor
mj_performer.foreground: Polished wooden dance floor, a folded rehearsal towel and a low unbranded stage monitor.
mj_performer.midground: Curtained practice platform, paired copper light stands and an upright piano with its lid closed.
mj_performer.background: Tall arched windows, indigo acoustic drapes and abstract geometric plaster reliefs unique to Multiverse Breach.
mj_performer.lighting: Warm overhead work lights crossed by soft violet window fill; no trademark concert lighting reconstruction.
mj_performer.sourceContext: Current HEROES_DB identifies King of Pop Avatar as a Multiverse Breach original tribute persona, not historical Michael Jackson or an official Moonwalker or Thriller incarnation. This is an original setting for that existing variant. A Michael Jackson 1:1 correction needs a separately selected source incarnation and its reference images; this brief does not claim one.

rhythm_guard_mj.location: Original lakeside covered soundcheck pavilion with a compact mixing station
rhythm_guard_mj.foreground: Weatherproof cable mat, a wired handheld microphone and a low road case beside the companion’s feet.
rhythm_guard_mj.midground: Open timber pavilion, modest speaker pair and a portable unbranded mixing desk.
rhythm_guard_mj.background: Still lake, reeds and a tree-lined bank beneath an open evening sky; no borrowed music-video set.
rhythm_guard_mj.lighting: Soft coral sunset behind the lake and practical amber lamps under the pavilion roof.
rhythm_guard_mj.sourceContext: Current HEROES_DB identifies Rhythm Guard as an original Multiverse Breach companion and stage persona. It is not an official Michael Jackson character, historical associate or second Michael Jackson incarnation. Keep this identity honest and use the existing project design as its reference; its visual review remains pending.

bob_minions.location: London toy-shop doorstep with a deep Georgian shop window
bob_minions.foreground: Bob’s Tim teddy bear, a worn stone step and a small fallen paper ribbon at Minion scale.
bob_minions.midground: A dark green shop door and a recessed display of simple wooden toys behind leaded glass.
bob_minions.background: A curving row of brick townhouses and an iron garden fence, with no crown or royal throne.
bob_minions.lighting: Clear mild morning light, warm shop-window glow and soft blue pavement shadows.
bob_minions.sourceContext: Minions, animated film 2015: London adventure Bob in ordinary blue denim overalls with silver double goggles and heterochromia. Original London street scene, not an exact shop seen in the film. His very short bald silhouette and Tim stay distinct from Kevin and Stuart.

kevin_minions.location: Thames embankment service stair beneath a London stone bridge
kevin_minions.foreground: A banana on a folded paper wrapper, damp stone paving and a heavy mooring ring.
kevin_minions.midground: Broad stone stair, black iron railing and bridge abutment give the tall Kevin a clean silhouette.
kevin_minions.background: River barges, masonry arches and distant London roofs; retain the film’s period rather than modern glass towers.
kevin_minions.lighting: Bright cloudy river light with pale sky bounce and small warm reflections off the stone.
kevin_minions.sourceContext: Minions, animated film 2015: London crown-heist-era Kevin at normal size in denim overalls, two brown eyes and upright central hair tuft. Original riverside rest scene; bridge geometry is not asserted to reproduce a film location.

stuart_minions.location: Palace-garden music platform with a red electric guitar on its stand
stuart_minions.foreground: Low wooden platform edge, curled guitar lead and a compact amplifier without a visible brand.
stuart_minions.midground: Stuart’s red guitar with white pickguard, modest microphone stand and neatly trimmed hedge border.
stuart_minions.background: Formal lawn, clipped topiary and a distant pale-stone palace façade, distinct from Bob’s shop and Kevin’s riverside stair.
stuart_minions.lighting: Golden celebratory afternoon sun with soft green garden bounce and restrained platform spotlights.
stuart_minions.sourceContext: Minions, animated film 2015: Stuart’s London rock-star finale incarnation, one brown eye, sparse parted hair and normal denim outfit. Original garden-performance composition; exact guitar form should be checked against the retained source reference, without turning him into a new musician character.

jack_sparrow_potc.location: Weathered Tortuga cargo wharf beside a moored Caribbean sloop
jack_sparrow_potc.foreground: Wet planks, thick hemp rope, a split rum barrel and barnacled timber posts.
jack_sparrow_potc.midground: A gangplank, stacked cargo crates, coarse sailcloth and the low gunwale of a wooden sailing vessel.
jack_sparrow_potc.background: Dense harbor masts, crooked tavern balconies and a dark palm-lined shore.
jack_sparrow_potc.lighting: Amber lanterns under a violet dusk sky, with cool harbor reflections on Jack’s coat.
jack_sparrow_potc.sourceContext: The Curse of the Black Pearl, film 2003: Jack’s red bandanna, worn tricorn, beaded hair, original coat, sword, flintlock and ordinary compass. Original Tortuga-compatible dock arrangement, not a later-film harbor or an exact screen reconstruction. Compass remains a personal prop.

roger_rabbit.location: Maroon Cartoon Studio soundstage containing a half-built toon kitchen set
roger_rabbit.foreground: A real wooden stage floor, coiled studio cable and a painted cartoon rolling pin at the border of the set.
roger_rabbit.midground: A deliberately exaggerated toon oven and cupboards stand beside exposed timber set bracing and a practical studio light.
roger_rabbit.background: Dark soundstage rafters, rolled canvas backdrops and a partly open freight door.
roger_rabbit.lighting: Warm theatrical key light on Roger with cooler practical fill exposing the live-action production space.
roger_rabbit.sourceContext: Who Framed Roger Rabbit, film 1988: Roger’s white toon body, orange tuft, red overalls, blue polka-dot bow tie and yellow gloves. Original studio composition combining toon objects and live-action surroundings, consistent with the film’s visual premise; no exact kitchen gag is claimed.

cyber_spider_electro_beam.location: Insect-scale electrical-test bench inside Kelly’s laboratory world
cyber_spider_electro_beam.foreground: Oversized insulated wire ends, a metal probe tip and scored rubber bench mat dwarf the small spider.
cyber_spider_electro_beam.midground: A low rack of ceramic insulators and a grounded test plate form a navigable path around the same Kelly spider’s Electro-Beam leg.
cyber_spider_electro_beam.background: Tall oscilloscope housing, cable bundles and unfocused laboratory shelving, without readable displays.
cyber_spider_electro_beam.lighting: Cool white task light with a restrained cyan reflection from the attachment; no human-sized gun beam.
cyber_spider_electro_beam.sourceContext: Spider: The Video Game, PlayStation 1997: this is Dr. Michael Kelly’s same cybernetic-spider protagonist in the Electro-Beam loadout, not a separate character. Original bench layout; precise body, weapon-leg model, emission and scale require original manual or gameplay reference. The layout is not advertised as a certified game level.

cyber_spider_flamethrower.location: Insect-scale warm-air maintenance duct behind laboratory heating equipment
cyber_spider_flamethrower.foreground: Dust grains, a small loose screw and the folded edge of a metal filter frame establish miniature scale.
cyber_spider_flamethrower.midground: A vent grille, copper heating pipe and shallow drip tray create a narrow path for Kelly’s Flamethrower Cyber-Leg loadout.
cyber_spider_flamethrower.background: A curved service duct recedes behind layered louvers and soft industrial haze.
cyber_spider_flamethrower.lighting: Warm pipe glow and dim amber maintenance light; a short localized attachment flame may provide a small additional highlight after reference review.
cyber_spider_flamethrower.sourceContext: Spider: The Video Game, PlayStation 1997: the same Kelly cybernetic spider carries the Flamethrower leg. Original industrial-service environment; neither the duct geometry nor an exact weapon effect is asserted as a source level. No humanoid flame warrior or invented extra protagonist.

raven_tt.location: Quiet meditation recess within Titans Tower with a broad bay window
raven_tt.foreground: A circular dark meditation mat, closed books and a low unlit candle holder.
raven_tt.midground: Simple built-in shelves and an angular window bench leave negative space around Raven’s blue-violet cloak.
raven_tt.background: A restrained view over Jump City’s bay from the Tower, with the city reduced to the series’ graphic shapes.
raven_tt.lighting: Cool moonlight, muted violet interior shadow and a small soft red reflection near her clasp; no generic neon laboratory.
raven_tt.sourceContext: Teen Titans, original animated series 2003-2006: gray skin, short violet hair, forehead gem and original cloaked costume. Original meditation scene inside the Tower, using the series’ design vocabulary. No claim that the room arrangement matches a particular episode.

starfire_tt.location: Open elevated waterfront transit platform in Jump City
starfire_tt.foreground: Graphic pale concrete paving, a simple bench and a windblown paper cup kept clear of Starfire’s boots.
starfire_tt.midground: Curved transit canopy, rounded support columns and an empty elevated track segment.
starfire_tt.background: Bright bay water, stylized waterfront towers and low green hills in the original series’ angular city design.
starfire_tt.lighting: Crisp peach morning light with cool cyan bay reflections and optional source-green starbolt light from her hands.
starfire_tt.sourceContext: Teen Titans, original animated series 2003-2006: orange skin, long red hair, green eyes, purple top and skirt with silver bracers. Original Jump City transport setting; not a named episode location or Teen Titans Go redesign. Her abilities remain green hand-emitted starbolts.

batman_tdk.location: Unfinished Gotham high-rise floor overlooking a nighttime construction zone
batman_tdk.foreground: Raw concrete slab, a loop of rebar and a low stack of dusty formwork panels.
batman_tdk.midground: Open structural columns, temporary safety mesh and a single construction lamp, with a clear ledge for the cape silhouette.
batman_tdk.background: Dense realistic Gotham windows, a distant tower crane and the black void of an unfinished elevator shaft.
batman_tdk.lighting: Cold city light mixed with harsh amber work lamps, catching the black segmented armor and gold belt.
batman_tdk.sourceContext: The Dark Knight, film 2008: Nolan’s Bruce Wayne in the segmented Batsuit. Original construction-floor composition compatible with the film’s realistic Gotham; exact props and costume require film-frame comparison. Keep grapnel and batarangs distinct from ordinary firearms.

harry.location: Room of Requirement training chamber with tall leaded windows and practice cushions
harry.foreground: Stone floor with a few loose dueling cushions and a plain wand-training stand.
harry.midground: Open practice space, high wall mirror and shelves of closed unmarked books.
harry.background: The room’s tall arched stonework and stacked chairs fade into a cool atmospheric recess.
harry.lighting: Pale winter daylight through the windows with a restrained wand-tip glow; no green Killing Curse.
harry.sourceContext: Order of the Phoenix, film 2007: fifth-year Harry in Gryffindor school clothing, round glasses, scar and holly wand. Original Dumbledore’s Army rehearsal scene. Film room details and costume still need frame review; any corporeal Patronus must be a stag.

hermione.location: Sheltered Hogwarts courtyard arcade beside a stone garden basin
hermione.foreground: An open unlettered study notebook, a closed book and fallen leaves on a stone bench.
hermione.midground: Gothic covered arcade, a modest stone basin and a column framing Hermione’s vine-wand silhouette.
hermione.background: A small enclosed green courtyard, slate roof and misted school windows beyond the arches.
hermione.lighting: Soft late-autumn afternoon light reflected off pale stone, with warm light under the arcade roof.
hermione.sourceContext: Order of the Phoenix, film 2007: fifth-year Hermione in Gryffindor school clothing with her vine wand. Original study-and-practice scene compatible with Hogwarts, not a reconstructed shot or later forest scene. No Time-Turner is added to this incarnation.

batman_n52.location: Gotham elevated railway signal roof above a deserted intersection
batman_n52.foreground: Rain-dark corrugated metal, a signal junction box and riveted rooftop edging.
batman_n52.midground: Overhead rail supports, a square signal gantry and a broken maintenance floodlight.
batman_n52.background: Dense comic-book Gotham stone façades and the sweeping curve of an elevated train line.
batman_n52.lighting: Blue storm-night ambient light, small amber signal reflections and sharp ink-like shadow shapes.
batman_n52.sourceContext: Batman: Endgame, New 52 Batman issues 35-40: ordinary gray Batsuit, white comic eye lenses and gold belt. Original Gotham transit setting; do not certify it as an issue panel. Keep this design separate from Nolan’s segmented suit, Justice Buster and Grim Knight firearms; costume requires panel comparison.

harley_n52.location: Belle Reve transport-loading bay with a reinforced security gate
harley_n52.foreground: Concrete floor, a low steel wheel chock and Harley’s oversized mallet resting clear of her feet.
harley_n52.midground: Reinforced double doors, a caged equipment locker and the rear corner of an unmarked prison transport.
harley_n52.background: Layered chain-link partitions, exposed pipes and a narrow exterior view of humid green scrub.
harley_n52.lighting: Flat cool institutional light broken by a warm strip of daylight through the loading gate.
harley_n52.sourceContext: Suicide Squad, New 52 volume 4 issue 1, 2011: early red-and-blue costume and split blue/red hair. Original Belle Reve-associated loading scene, not asserted as a page from issue 1. Match the exact source-panel costume before visual approval; no Rebirth or 2016 movie substitution.

joker_n52.location: Abandoned Gotham municipal-clinic corridor with an overturned examination trolley
joker_n52.foreground: Cracked floor tiles, scattered blank examination folders and a fallen chrome tray.
joker_n52.midground: Peeling pale-green walls, frosted treatment-room doors and a trolley with small sealed unlabelled vials.
joker_n52.background: A long corridor recedes to shuttered glass doors and a dim stairwell.
joker_n52.lighting: Sickly fluorescent ceiling pools mixed with cool dawn from a high window, emphasizing his restored white face.
joker_n52.sourceContext: Batman: Endgame, New 52 Batman issues 35-40: Joker with restored face, green hair and the matching issue-era civilian costume. Original threatening Gotham clinic scene evokes the arc’s toxin crisis without claiming an actual panel or inventing source events. Exact clothing, knife and toxin containers require panel review; no strapped-on Death of the Family face.

han_solo.location: Recessed repair alcove at the edge of a Mos Eisley docking hangar
han_solo.foreground: Coarse beige sand, a coiled fuel hose and a shallow mechanic’s parts tray.
han_solo.midground: Curved plaster docking wall, thick hangar doorway and a simple servicing trolley near Han’s holstered DL-44.
han_solo.background: A partial view of the Millennium Falcon’s weathered hull and the high rim of the open desert hangar.
han_solo.lighting: Hard warm Tatooine daylight above, soft cool shade in the repair alcove.
han_solo.sourceContext: A New Hope, film 1977: young Han with cream shirt, black vest, blue trousers with red side stripes and right-thigh DL-44 holster. Original Mos Eisley hangar composition inspired by the source setting; no exact docking-bay shot or later-film costume is claimed.

luke.location: Recessed control gantry beside the Death Star II throne-room approach
luke.foreground: Black gridded walkway, low rail and a dark angular control pedestal without readable symbols.
luke.midground: Shallow stair run, tall Imperial window supports and layered control consoles.
luke.background: Deep station shaft and a distant circular observation-window structure reveal restrained stars beyond.
luke.lighting: Cool blue-gray Imperial interior light with localized green reflection from Luke’s single lightsaber.
luke.sourceContext: Return of the Jedi, film 1983: young Luke in the black duel outfit with gloved mechanical right hand and green saber. Original arrangement of Death Star II throne-room architecture, not an exact film frame. Keep location and outfit within the locked Jedi Knight incarnation.

vader.location: Carbon-freezing chamber service platform in Cloud City on Bespin
vader.foreground: Dark metal grating, low pipe joints and condensed vapor rolling over the platform edge.
vader.midground: Industrial support columns, orange-lit machinery wells and descending angular railings.
vader.background: Tall blue-black shaft walls and layered carbon-freezing machinery partly obscured by vapor.
vader.lighting: Strong amber underlight through the floor grates and cold blue overhead light, with a small red saber reflection.
vader.sourceContext: The Empire Strikes Back, film 1980: Vader’s closed helmet, life-support armor, cape and red lightsaber. Original adjacent service-platform composition within the Bespin carbon-freezing setting. Exact control-box details and chamber architecture still require film-frame comparison; no exposed Anakin face.

grim_knight.location: Fortified Gotham police checkpoint in a drained flood-control channel
grim_knight.foreground: Shallow puddles, concrete debris and sandbag corners surrounding a low firing barrier.
grim_knight.midground: Steel checkpoint gates, a reinforced police booth and a heavy unmarked equipment case.
grim_knight.background: Massive retaining walls, storm-drain mouths and distant Gotham blocks under overcast sky.
grim_knight.lighting: Cold storm daylight and a single harsh white searchlight, preserving dark tactical-armor texture.
grim_knight.sourceContext: The Batman Who Laughs: The Grim Knight issue 1, 2019: armed Dark Multiverse Bruce Wayne. Original militarized Gotham setting motivated by his source identity, not a claimed one-shot location. Cowl, armor, ammunition mounts and every weapon model require direct issue-panel reference; do not use the Batman Who Laughs visor.

cyber_spider_kelly.location: Insect-scale specimen-preparation station beside a laboratory microscope
cyber_spider_kelly.foreground: A clean glass slide, a steel scalpel laid flat and a clipped paper tab make Kelly’s mechanical spider visibly tiny.
cyber_spider_kelly.midground: Raised microscope base, a shallow specimen dish and textured cork pad form a traversable bench surface for the default Slasher loadout.
cyber_spider_kelly.background: Oversized focus knobs, amber reagent bottles and softly receding laboratory cupboards.
cyber_spider_kelly.lighting: Neutral white microscope task light with soft amber glass reflections and grounded mechanical shadows.
cyber_spider_kelly.sourceContext: Spider: The Video Game, PlayStation 1997: Dr. Michael Kelly’s cybernetic-spider body with the default Slasher attachment. This is the base equipment presentation of the same protagonist used in the Electro-Beam and Flamethrower entries, not a third person. Original laboratory bench layout; source body and attachment details require manual or gameplay review.
